image.hold_hint: Hold the mouse button on the preview, or hold Space, to see the original
image.original_title: Original (let go to see the notes again)
image.kinds_all: PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP, BMP or TIFF
image.player_tip: Your player's window size and how many keys it shows across (Falling notes) or up (Piano roll). The outline is as many px in the player's window: the preview is a different size, so it draws the outline thinner or thicker to look the same.
image.shade: Shading (bright to dark across the key)
image.look_note: The look only changes the preview, so it matches the player you use. "Join same-colour notes" changes the notes too: joined = fewer, longer notes.
image.cancelled: Cancelled: the image and its settings are back as they were.
image.still_making: The image is still being made: wait for it to finish, or press Cancel.
image.big:
This image makes a grid of {rows:,} × {cols:,} = {cells:,} cells, so up to {cells:,} notes. Making it may take about {secs} s; you can cancel it while it's made.

Fewer keys or steps per key make it smaller.
image.no_memory: There wasn't enough memory to make this image, so it's back as it was. Fewer keys or steps per key make a smaller one.
image.drag: ⠿  Drag me into the piano roll
image.use10_project: On for the whole project: "Use channel 10" is ticked under Multi channel.
image.use10_tip: 16 colours: colour 10 goes on channel 10. Many players draw its notes, but they play no sound (or drums).
image.share_note: {n} other placed image(s) share these colours. More share = this image gets the better colours when they compete.
image.share_alone: Share only matters with other images placed (they all share one set of colours).
image.others_missing: ({n} other image(s) couldn't be read: their colours may shift)
image.changed_ask:
The image file has changed since you placed it:
{path}

Yes = use the new version (the placed image is made again from it).
No = keep the current one (the placed image stays as it is).
image.shape_ask:
This image has another shape than the placed one.

Yes = keep the image's own shape.
No = stretch it to the placed size.
image.panel: An image: {value:,} notes. Double-click it to change its look. Drag a corner or side to resize it (its notes are made again from the image, sharp), just outside a corner to turn it, just outside a side's middle to skew it.
image.label: {name}  ·  {keys} keys  ·  {colours} colours  ·  double-click: look
image.menu_own_shape: Back to the image's own shape
image.swatch_tip: Click a colour to pick it yourself: it stays as you picked it (corner mark). Right-click: let Spiderweb pick it again.
velocity_formula.pattern_tip: The pattern along the line. Your saved patterns (Formula → Pattern along the line → Custom…) are in the list too.
velocity_formula.loops_tip: How many times the pattern repeats between the line's two ends. Parts of a loop work too (4.5).
velocity_formula.number_tip: "{name}" in the pattern's formula, in velocity steps (a Wave of height 20 goes up to 20 above the line and 20 below it).
graph_window.drag_a_point_to_move_it:
Drag a point to move it (Shift = free). Click anywhere to add a point, right-click a point to type its value or delete it. Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y undo / redo here.
100 % = the number in the box; the bumps change along the line as the graph does.
graph_window.x_0_at_the_line_s: x = 0 at the line's start, 1 at its end; the result is in %. E.g. 100*x   50+50*sin(x*2*pi)
graph_window.it_doesn_t_give_a_number: it doesn't give a number everywhere from x = 0 to 1
graph_window.select_a_line_with_tumours_: Select a line with tumours to give its {name} a graph.
graph_window.box_is_zero: {label} is 0 in the tumour window, so this graph changes nothing. Type a number there first.
tumour_window.how_far_the_bumps_stick_ou: How far the bumps stick out, in keys (as the piano roll looks).
tumour_window.how_long_each_bump_is_alon:
How long each bump is along the line, in ticks.
0 = spikes: every bump is one point pushed sideways,
and the line zigzags straight from spike to spike.
tumour_window.from_the_start_of_one_bump:
From the start of one bump to the start of the next, in ticks.
A bump longer than this is cut where the next one starts.
tumour_window.smooth_start_and_end_over_:
Smooth start and end: over this many ticks from each end of the range,
the bumps grow from nothing to full size (and shrink back to nothing at the end),
so the line leads into them instead of starting with a sudden side.
0 = off.
tumour_window.tilts_every_bump_its_two_f:
Tilts every bump, its two feet staying on the line.
Plus leans it forward (the way the line runs), minus leans it back.
90 lays it flat along the line, 180 turns it over to the other side.
tumour_window.square_bumps_only_slants_t:
Square bumps only: slants the square's sides.
0 = a square, 100 = the top narrows to a point (like a triangle),
minus = the top is wider than the bottom (the sides lean outwards).
tumour_window.which_side_of_the_line_the: Which side of the line the bumps go (left / right as you go along the line from its start).
tumour_window.only_matters_where_the_lin:
Only matters where the line curves under a bump (long bumps on a curve, arc or circle).
Straight: each bump sits on a straight shortcut between its ends (angular).
Bent with the line: each bump follows the curve under it (stays round).
tumour_window.only_this_part_of_the_line: Only this part of the line gets bumps (0 % = its start, 100 % = its end).
tumour_window.fit_the_bumps_evenly_the_d:
Fit the bumps evenly: the distance is changed a little so a whole number of them fits
the range exactly, with the last one landing right on its end.
On a closed loop (like a full circle) the bumps meet up seamlessly where it starts
(alternating sides: an even number, so they keep alternating there too).
tumour_window.select_a_line_polyline_fre: Select a line, polyline, freehand stroke, curve or arc to give it tumours.
tumour_window.a_graph_this_number_change: A graph: this number changes along the line.
tumour_window.tip_reset: Every setting back to its default and no graphs (tumours stay on or off). Accept keeps the change, X or Esc puts the lines back as they were.
tumour_window.shapes_with_tumours_the_se: {n} shapes, {on} with tumours: the settings change those. Clicking the half-ticked Tumours box gives the others these tumours too.
tumour_window.the_joined_shapes_kept_the: The joined shapes kept their own tumours (these are the first one's). Changing anything here, even just switching Tumours off and on, gives the WHOLE curve these settings and the other shapes' tumours are gone (Ctrl+Z brings them back).
tumour_window.bumps_along_the_line_the_l: Bumps along the line. The line's points stay draggable. Length 0 = spikes (a zigzag).
tumour_window.tick_tumours_to_put_bumps_: Tick Tumours to put bumps along this line.
layers.title: Layers
layers.hidden_warn: {n} hidden (Layers): left out of the shape.
layers.all_hidden_state: Every stroke is hidden (Layers): nothing to place.
layers.all_hidden: Every stroke is hidden. Show at least one (the eye in Layers) to use the shape.
drawer.mirror_tip: New strokes get a mirrored copy across the board's middle: Horizontal = left ↔ right, Vertical = top ↔ bottom, Both = all four corners. The grey side shows where the copy goes. Halves that meet on the mirror line join up into one outline.
drawer.name: Name
drawer.export_tip: Copies this drawing to the clipboard as text, to share. Paste the text anywhere; whoever copies it presses Import.
drawer.import_tip: Adds a drawing shared as text (copy the whole line first) to your shape library.
drawer.exported: Copied "{name}" to the clipboard as text. Paste it anywhere to share it.
drawer.exported_long: It's {chars:,} characters long: it may be too long to paste in some places.
drawer.import_none: The clipboard doesn't hold a shared drawing. Copy the whole line first (someone makes it with Export in the drawer).
drawer.import_shapes: The clipboard holds shared shapes, not a drawing. Close the drawer and press Ctrl+V on the piano roll to paste them.
drawer.import_broken: The shared text on the clipboard is cut off or changed, so it can't be imported. Copy the whole line again.
drawer.import_newer: This shared drawing was made by a newer Spiderweb. Update Spiderweb to import it.
drawer.clipboard_busy: Couldn't use the clipboard (another program has it open). Try again.
drawer.mouse_x_y_grid_squares_from: Mouse: x {u:+.1f}, y {v:+.1f} grid squares from the middle
drawer.the_middle_anchor_of_a_symmetric: The middle anchor of a symmetric curve stays (turn Symmetric halves off to remove it).
drawer.the_current_drawing_isn_t_saved: The current drawing isn't saved. Throw it away?
drawer.unsaved_quit:
The drawing in the shape drawer isn't saved.
Close Spiderweb anyway and lose it?
drawer.is_built_in_and_can_t: "{name}" is built in and can't be deleted.
drawer.the_built_in_comes_back_in: The built-in "{built_in_name}" comes back in its place.
drawer.delete_from_the_library_shapes_al:
Delete "{name}" from the library?
Shapes already placed on the piano roll stay as they are.
drawer.give_the_shape_a_name_first: Give the shape a name first.
drawer.is_already_in_the_library_replace:
"{name}" is already in the library. Replace it?
Shapes already placed on the piano roll stay as they are.
drawer.deleted_in_use: Deleted "{name}" from the shape library: the Custom shape tool now uses Circle.
drawer.changed_elsewhere: "{name}" was saved somewhere else (for example from the piano roll) after you opened it here. Replace it with this drawing?
drawer.rename_tip: Gives the picked shape a new name (F2, or click its name again). Shapes already placed on the piano roll keep their old name.
drawer.is_built_in_rename: "{name}" is built in and can't be renamed.
drawer.closed_shape_empty_fill_and_spam: Closed shape: Empty, Fill and Spam all work.
drawer.one_gap_red_dots_fill_and: One gap (red dots): Fill and Spam close it with a straight line.
drawer.open_ends_red_dots_fill_and: Open ends (red dots): Fill and Spam close each gap with a straight line.
drawer.nothing_to_fill: Only outline-only lines and fill lines: Fill and Spam have nothing to fill.
drawer.only_coloured_filled: Only outline-only lines and fill lines: Fill and Spam fill only the coloured areas.
drawer.slice_nothing: Nothing cut: the line has to cross a stroke (a closed one all the way through).
drawer.split_closed: Split here (closed line: use the Slice tool)
drawer.split_nothing: Nothing split: that spot is the stroke's end.
drawer.area_colour: Colour for the areas you click:
drawer.area_normal: As normal: filled or not like Fill and Spam do it
drawer.area_outside: That's outside the drawing: click an area inside it.
drawer.colours_used: Colours used: {n} of {most} ({m} with "Outline" on). The shape's own colour counts too.
drawer.colours_too_many: That's more than a shape can have: on the piano roll the extra colours share the last one.
drawer.areas_reset_ask: Put every area back to normal (filled or not like Fill and Spam do it)? All the colours and Empty areas you gave are removed. You can undo this.
drawer.areas_none_coloured: No area has a colour yet.
panel_pattern.loops_tip: How many times the pattern repeats along the line. Parts of a loop work too (4.5).
panel_pattern.loops_most: {most} loops is the most a line can have.
panel_pattern.number_tip: "{name}" in the pattern's formula. Sizes to the side are in keys.
panel_pattern.number_tip_polygon: "{name}" in the pattern's formula. Sizes to the side are in hundredths of the polygon's height.
panel_pattern.number_tip_drawer: "{name}" in the pattern's formula. Sizes to the side are in hundredths of the board.
panel_pattern.across_all_tip: The loops carry on from piece to piece, evenly spaced over the whole joined curve.
panel_pattern.each_piece_tip: Every piece of the joined curve gets all the loops on its own.
panel_pattern.baking: Turning it into a plain curve…
panel_pattern.plain_big: The plain curve would have {n} points. A curve this big makes the piano roll slow while it's selected.
pattern.can_t_work_it_out_at: it can't be worked out at x = {x}
pattern.loops_taken: "loops" is the Loops box: give that number another name
pattern.can_t_work_it_out_at_t: it can't be worked out at t = {t}
pattern.it_s_just_a_dot: it's just a dot (it has no size)
pattern_dialog.shape_help:
t goes from 0 to 1 while the shape is drawn. The drawing is fitted to the curve: if it ends where it started (like a circle), it's as wide as from the curve's start A to its end B; if not, it starts at A and ends at B. It follows the curve, so bending the dotted curve bends the shape.
Works: numbers, t, + - * / ^ ( ), pi, e, sin cos tan asin acos atan sqrt exp ln log abs min max floor.
pattern_dialog.shape_edited_by_hand: Edited by hand. Its start and end points stay where they are (their handles can move).
pattern_dialog.whole_shape: The whole shape, between the curve's ends A and B. Drag a point to change it by hand; double-click the line to add a point, right-click a point to remove it. Alt + drag: a sharp corner. Wheel = zoom, drag empty space = move.
pattern_dialog.title: Pattern along the line
pattern_dialog.name: Name
pattern_dialog.along_tip: Can be left empty. Moves the line forward (+) or back (-) along the curve, in loops (1 = a whole loop). Where it goes back faster than the loop moves on, the line runs back over itself and makes curls.
pattern_dialog.sym_tip: Symmetric halves: only the first half of the formula counts. The second half is made from it, mirrored (like an arch) or turned half way round (like an S).
pattern_dialog.edit_formula_tip: Type your own formula. Any name in it other than x (like height) gets its own number box.
pattern_dialog.help:
One loop: x goes from 0 at its start to 1 at its end; y is how far to the side of the curve, in keys (up on a curve going to the right).
Works: numbers, x, + - * / ^ ( ), pi, e, sin cos tan asin acos atan sqrt exp ln log abs min max floor.
pattern_dialog.help_polygon:
One loop: x goes from 0 at its start to 1 at its end; y is how far to the side (outward), in hundredths of the polygon's height. Every side gets the pattern, and it grows and shrinks with the polygon.
Works: numbers, x, + - * / ^ ( ), pi, e, sin cos tan asin acos atan sqrt exp ln log abs min max floor.
pattern_dialog.help_drawer:
One loop: x goes from 0 at its start to 1 at its end; y is how far to the side of the curve, in hundredths of the board (100 = the whole board). The drawing keeps these sizes when it's placed, so they grow and shrink with it.
Works: numbers, x, + - * / ^ ( ), pi, e, sin cos tan asin acos atan sqrt exp ln log abs min max floor.
pattern_dialog.fit_view_tip: Show all of it again. Mouse wheel = zoom in and out; drag empty space (or middle-drag) = move around.
pattern_dialog.back_to_formula_tip: Forget the changes made by hand: the loop follows the formula again.
pattern_dialog.name_first: Give the pattern a name first.
pattern_dialog.only_saved: Only your saved patterns can be deleted (the grey ones come with Spiderweb).
pattern_dialog.edited_by_hand: Edited by hand: every loop along the line follows this one.
pattern_dialog.one_loop: One loop, as long as it is on the curve. Drag a point to change it by hand; double-click the line to add a point, right-click a point to remove it. Alt + drag: a sharp corner. Wheel = zoom, drag empty space = move.
claw.n_shapes: {n} shapes (they all get the same settings)
claw.tip_mode:
How the notes are picked:
By time: cuts slices of time out, like the claw machine of other piano rolls.
Count notes / keys / chords: keep some, trash some, over and over (notes starting together = one chord).
Random: keeps notes picked at random.
claw.tip_keep: How many to keep before trashing some.
claw.tip_skip: How many to throw away after the ones kept. 0 = keep everything.
claw.tip_pct: About this many notes in every hundred stay; which ones is random.
claw.tip_new_random: Pick other notes at random (the same number of them).
claw.tip_shorten: The notes picked to go stay, only shorter.
claw.tip_cut: How long they stay: this much of their length (at least 1 tick).
claw.tip_period: The claw works on this much time at a time, over and over, starting at the shape's first note.
claw.tip_trash:
Cuts each period into equal slices and throws one away: 1/4 = the first quarter, 2/4 = the second quarter, and so on.
Notes in it go, notes crossing its edges are cut, and the later notes move earlier to close the gap.
claw.tip_dist_box: Or type a value from -100 to 100 in the box beside it (1/3 or 50*2/3 work too).
claw.tip_dist:
Bends time inside each period.
Right: long notes first, then faster and faster. Left: the other way round.
Drag up / down (Shift = fine), mouse wheel or arrow keys; it stops at 0 for a moment on the way past.
Right mouse button: points it at the mouse. Middle-click (press the wheel) = back to 0.
claw.tip_stretch: Stretches the result back to the shape's full length (the notes get longer too).
claw.tip_short: Removes notes the claw left very short (under 1/24 beat). Notes that were that short already stay.
claw.tip_reset: Everything back to the start (the claw then changes nothing).
range_window.title: Spam gate range
range_window.from_tip: The first gate: where the graph is at the bottom. It's the shape's spam gate (the gate box in the side panel).
range_window.to_tip: The second gate: where the graph reaches the top.
range_window.dir_tip: Left to right: every key is cut at the same places, the gate changing over time. Low to high / Top to bottom: each key has its own gate, from the lowest key to the highest, or from the highest to the lowest.
range_window.rows_tip: Every key row goes from the first gate to the second along its own length, short or long, instead of along the whole shape. Where a row crosses the shape more than once, each piece runs the whole range. A row too short for any note gets one note of the first gate. Left to right only.
range_window.join_tip: A row that crosses the shape more than once runs the range once, from its first piece to its last, gaps included, instead of starting over on each piece.
range_window.fit_tip: Each row's first and last note reach exactly to the shape's edges: stretched over the blank left at an end, or trimmed where a long gate would stick out.
range_window.smooth_tip: Every whole-tick gate between the two can be used.
range_window.steps_tip: The gate only halves or doubles from the first one (the first, half of it, a quarter…), so the shape is made of sections of equal notes. The graph still says where each step comes.
range_window.evenly_tip: The gate changes evenly from the line start to the wall, as the graph says.
range_window.with_curve_tip: The graph runs along how far the funnel has opened instead of along its length: the gate stays near the first one along the line and changes fast where the funnel opens up. Funnels only.
range_window.hint: Bottom = the first gate, top = the second. Drag a point to move it (Shift = free), click the line or empty space to add one, right-click a point to delete it. The pale steps are the whole-tick gates the notes get. Straight = every gate gets an equal share, so most notes are the short ones.
range_window.no_step: Steps: no halving or doubling of From fits up to To, so every note keeps the first gate.
chop.n_shapes: {n} shapes (they all get the same settings)
chop.tip_rhythm: The rhythm every note is cut into. It repeats along each note, as many times as fits.
chop.tip_save: Keep this rhythm under a name: it shows at the bottom of the Rhythm list from now on.
chop.no_pieces: No pieces in the rhythm: the notes aren't chopped.
chop.name_taken: "{name}" is a built-in rhythm's name. Pick another name:
chop.tip_strip: One repeat of the rhythm. Press on empty space to put a piece there, as loud as the mouse is high; drag to make it longer or change its velocity. Drag a piece up or down to make it louder or quieter (in %, the dotted line = the note's own velocity). Right-click (or right-drag) to delete pieces. Empty space = a gap in the notes.
chop.tip_grid: How many grid cells each step has in the strip above (3 for triplets). Only for drawing.
chop.tip_steps: How many steps one repeat of the rhythm lasts.
chop.tip_step_length: How long one step is: pick a note length here, or type it in ticks in the box beside it. Shorter = faster rhythm, more notes. Off (top of the list) = 1 tick, the shortest pieces there can be. Custom… = any length you set up.
chop.tip_ticks: One step's length in ticks. Type any whole number (1 = 1-tick pieces) or drag sideways, or pick a note length on the left.
chop.tip_velocity: Amount: how much the rhythm's own velocities count. 0 = every piece keeps its note's velocity, 100 = the rhythm's velocities fully.
chop.tip_mode: % of each note: every piece is a share of its note's own velocity, so velocity ramps stay. Fixed: every piece is exactly the velocity drawn. Switching keeps the pieces about as loud (100 % = 127).
chop.tip_absolute: On: the rhythm lines up with the song's beats, so a note starting between them gets a short first piece. Off: the rhythm starts again at each note's start.
chop.too_many: Too many pieces to make: the notes are left unchopped. Pick a longer step length.
chop.tip_reset: Back to the start: the Even rhythm, 1/16 steps.
chop.quick_done: Quick chop: notes cut into {snap} pieces. Right-click → Chop… (Alt+U) changes or removes it
strum.n_shapes: {n} shapes (they all get the same settings)
strum.tip_start: Switches the Start part on or off: when the notes start, and their velocity.
strum.tip_end: Switches the End part on or off: when the notes end.
strum.tip_time:
How much later each note starts than the one before (in ticks).
Right: the lowest note first. Left: the highest note first.
strum.tip_tension:
Right: small steps first, each one bigger. Left: big steps first, each one smaller.
100 = each step twice the last, -100 = half.
strum.tip_vel:
How much quieter each note is than the one before it (in velocity).
Left: the other way round, the last note keeps its velocity. Never under 1.
strum.tip_vel_tension: Right: small changes first, each one bigger. Left: big changes first, each one smaller.
strum.tip_end_time:
How much earlier each note ends than the next one (in ticks).
Right: the last note of the strum keeps its end. Left: the first one does.
strum.tip_end_tension: Right: small steps first, each one bigger. Left: big steps first, each one smaller.
strum.tip_preserve: The ends stay where they were: the notes get shorter instead of moving.
strum.tip_ahead: The strum happens before the chord: the last note lands where the chord started.
strum.tip_chop: Where a note starts while others are still held, those are cut there and strum again with it.
strum.tip_alternate: Every other chord strums the other way (notes on their own don't count).
strum.tip_reset: Everything back to the start (the strum then changes nothing).
strum.tip_knob: Drag up / down (Shift = fine), mouse wheel or arrow keys. Right mouse button: points it at the mouse. Middle-click = back to 0. Or type a value in the box under it.
path.tip_kind: The way the copies go from point to point. Curve and Arc bend a stretch through its round middle point: drag it on the piano roll. Dragging one on a straight path makes it a curve.
path.tip_formula: A pattern laid along the whole path, like a curve's Formula: the copies follow its waves. Loops = how many times it repeats from A to the last point.
path.tip_custom: Pick, change, draw or type the pattern along the path, and save your own.
path.tip_every: One copy for each time this much later the path goes, spread evenly along the line. On a straight line they start right on the beats, counted from where the shape starts. The last one ends at the path's end or before it.
path.tip_every_ticks: The same in ticks: type any length.
path.tip_count: This many copies in all (the shape itself is the first), spread evenly along the path's length. For paths that go back in time, like a loop.
path.tip_anchor:
Ticked: a copy's corner sits right on each point, and each part of the path is spaced on its own.
Unticked: the copies are spaced evenly along the whole path, straight through the points (a copy on top of an arc sits in its middle).
path.tip_half:
Where the path turns, the copies carry on past the point at their spacing, and only the parts on the near side of the point are kept, so the turn is as full as the rest of the path (Speed Even only). With Number of copies, the spacing is also kept the same on every part of the path.
Untick for whole copies only.
path.idle: Right-click a shape → Copy along a path… to start a new path, or click + above.
path.idle_differ: The selected shapes have different paths. Click + above to give them one new path together, or select one shape to see its paths.
path.tip_speed:
Even: the same distance between copies all the way.
Speed up: close together at A, further apart towards the end.
Slow down: the other way round.
path.tip_size0: How big the first copy is (the shape itself), in % of its size.
path.tip_size1: How big the last copy is. The copies in between grow or shrink step by step.
path.tip_colours:
Keep: every copy has the shape's own colours.
Shift all channels: each copy moves every colour on by Step channels, through all the channels.
Turn within own colours: each copy uses only the shape's own colours, moved on by Step.
One per copy: each copy is one colour, the next one Step channels on.
path.tip_step: How far each copy's colours move on from the copy before (minus = backwards).
path.needs_multi: Channels isn't Multi channel now: the copies stay in one channel, so the colours don't change.
path.tip_flip:
Each copy going down: the copies where the path goes down are flipped (the way picked beside it).
Mirror at the peak: past the path's first peak or dip, the copies are the ones before it mirrored. The copy on that spot is cut in half there.
path.tip_way: Which way the copies going down are flipped.
path.tip_top: Where copies cover each other, which one is drawn on top. The one under it is cut away there, note by note.
path.no_peak: The path has no peak or dip, so nothing is mirrored.
path.tip_inside: Only the notes from the Lowest key to the Highest key are kept, the shape's own too. The rest are cut off. These keys stay put when the shape moves (dotted lines on the piano roll).
path.tip_low: The lowest key notes are kept on (0 = the lowest key of the piano roll).
path.tip_high: The highest key notes are kept on.
path.tip_point: The point these boxes show. Click a point on the piano roll to pick it.
path.tip_bar: Where the point is: the bar (counted from 1, like the status line).
path.tip_beat: Where the point is: the beat in that bar (counted from 1).
path.tip_tick: Where the point is: the tick in that beat.
path.tip_key: Where the point is: the key (0 = the lowest).
path.tip_add_point: A new point after the last one: it follows the mouse on the piano roll until you click. Right-click a point to remove it.
path.click_b: Click on the piano roll where the path ends (B). Going up, A is the shape's bottom-left corner and B the last copy's top-right corner (going down: top-left and bottom-right). The copies follow the mouse until then.
path.click_point: Click on the piano roll where point {name} goes. Right-click to stop adding.
path.n_copies: {n} copies (the shape included). Drag the points or the round middle points on the piano roll. Right-click a point to remove it.
path.tip_plain: Every copy becomes a shape of its own (its notes), so you can move, cut or change each one by hand. The shape itself stays as it is, without this path. Closes the window.
path.plain_big: This makes {n} new shapes. That many can make the shapes list and editing slow.
path.tip_reset: Every point taken away: click on the piano roll again to place B.
tool_window.tip_new: A new page: change a setting and it goes on top of the shape's other pages, working on the notes they left. Click a numbered tab to change that page instead.
tool_window.differ: The selected shapes have different pages: a change goes on a new page on each.
tool_window.tip_on: Untick to switch this page off for now: it's kept, but changes nothing.
tool_window.tip_remove: Remove: takes this page off the selected shapes. The pages after it then work on the notes left before it.
tool_window.order:
This shape's pages, in order (each works on the notes the one before it left):
{steps}
between.title: Add between
between.steps_tip: How many in-between shapes go from the first shape to the last (not counting those two).
between.reverse_tip: Pairs the first shape's start with the last shape's end (and the other way round). Turn it on or off if the steps twist through each other.
between.colours_tip: Every shape of the group gets a channel of its own, the first and last shapes too. Past the number of colours they take turns. Needs Channels: Multi channel. A shape with Colours turned on keeps its own Colours.
between.turns_tip: How many colours the shapes take turns over (at most 15, 16 with "Use channel 10").
between.needs_multi: Channels isn't Multi channel now, so all the steps are in one channel and look the same.
between.hint: Left = the first shape, right = the last. Up = more like the last shape. Each pale line is a step. Drag a point to move it (Shift = free), click the line or empty space to add one, right-click a point to delete it.
between.preview_hint: Blue = the first shape, red = the last. Drag their points to change them (Shift = free); the steps follow. Click a shape's line to push it with the pad (yellow = the one pushed).
between.preview_hint_dark: Blue = the first shape, white = the last. Drag their points to change them (Shift = free); the steps follow. Click a shape's line to push it with the pad (yellow = the one pushed).
between.push_tip: Drag from the middle: the steps leave the picked shape this way, and the further out, the harder. Middle = no push (straight). The middle pulls the stick in; hold Shift to place it anywhere. Ctrl = 8 ways only. Double-click = no push.
between.smooth_tip: The steps go through each key shape without a corner, as if pushed along. Off = a corner at each key without a push of its own.
sustain.title: Sustain
sustain.on_tip:
Each note is held until the last note of its group on the same key ends, so notes pile up on top of each other. Made for lagging out MIDI players.
These notes keep their overlaps in every Channels mode; other shapes' notes still end where these start.
sustain.auto_each: Auto (each shape works out its own)
sustain.auto_tip:
Works out the gap from the shape's own notes: the most common gap between notes on a key, plus half of it.
Longer gaps are holes in the shape (like the inside of a ring) and stay empty, so the shape keeps its look.
sustain.nothing: No shape that can be sustained is selected.
sustain.own_tip: Gaps up to this long are held over. Make it bigger than a hole to hold across the hole too.
sustain.most_tip:
Each note is held to this length at most, instead of to the end of its group. It never goes past the group's end, so the shape keeps its look, and notes already longer stay as they are.
The number follows the PPQ.
sustain.every_tip:
The sustain stops this often, counted from the shape's first note: every note sounding there ends, and one new note per key starts on the same tick, so the sustain starts again with no gap.
A resized shape gets more or fewer stops. The number follows the PPQ.
sustain.stops_tip:
The sustain also stops at the points you put: every note sounding there ends, and one new note per key starts on the same tick.
The points stretch with the shape when it's resized. While the shape is selected, the piano roll shows them as lines: drag one to move it, right-click one to remove it. Right-click the shape for "Add sustain stop here", or double-click it while this window is open.
sustain.add_stop_tip: Puts a stop on the next snap line after the last stop (the first one: after the shape's start).
sustain.past_tip: A stop may go past the end of the shape's notes. Then the last notes on each key are held on until that stop, so the shape gets longer.
sustain.no_room: No room for another stop before the shape's end.
sustain.too_many: Too many stops for this many notes: the stops aren't put on. Use fewer stops.
sustain.not_here: A stop can't go there: it has to be inside the shape (or past its end with "Allow past the shape's end").
sustain.from_tip: Moves the stops later by this much, so they needn't line up with the shape's start.
